From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Scope:** Seller's "Key Negotiated Positions" and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded

Before the substance, one procedural matter. The Seller's package closes with a note stating that clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**That is not correct and should not be relied on.** Nothing in our instructions or the baseline terms records any such agreement. A [STANDARD] tag applied unilaterally by the other side's counsel is a negotiation device, not a record of agreement. Several of the most buyer-adverse positions in the entire package (liability caps, knowledge exclusion, fundamental warranties, Riverlark, Ironquay, the data incident) are precisely the ones marked [STANDARD]. I have reviewed every clause on its merits and recommend the response letter expressly state that no clause is agreed until the Buyer confirms in writing, and that the categorisation is not accepted.

---

## 1. Liability regime (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
A 20% cap on general warranties is at the low end but within the range seen in Australian mid-market deals (typically 20–50%, sometimes 100% where W&I is not used). Whether it is acceptable depends on (a) whether we obtain W&I insurance and (b) how the specific risks below are carved out. **Position:** push for 30–50%, or accept 20% only if (i) all identified-risk items are covered by specific indemnities outside the cap and (ii) fundamental, title and tax warranties sit at 100% of price.

### 1.2 De minimis and basket
- De minimis of AUD 25,000 is roughly 0.1% of price – acceptable in isolation, but it should apply to *series of related claims* on an aggregated basis (so the Seller cannot fragment one problem into sub-threshold items – note the three AUD 110,000 Sandbar renewals, which look structured in exactly that way).
- Basket of AUD 250,000 (~1%) is market. However, the Seller proposes an **excess-only (deductible) basket**. Buyer position should be a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). If we concede a deductible, the cap should move up accordingly.

### 1.3 Time limits – 18 months, applied to "all Claims"
18 months for general warranties is short but not unusual; we should seek 24 months (allowing two audit cycles). The more serious problem is the second sentence: **"any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** Combined with the proposal below, this would subject title, capacity, tax and indemnity claims to an 18-month window and a 20% cap. Tax should run to the later of 7 years or expiry of the Commissioner's amendment period; title/capacity should be unlimited or at least 6–7 years.

### 1.4 Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps
**This is a material departure from market and from the Buyer's interests. Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If the Seller does not own the shares, or lacks capacity to sell, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing and the remedy would be capped at AUD 4.8m and extinguished after 18 months. Title and capacity warranties must be capped at 100% of the purchase price (plus costs) with a long-stop of at least 6 years, and must not be qualified by disclosure.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"
Also reject. The limitation package should apply to Warranty Claims only. Specific indemnities, fraud, wilful concealment, leakage/completion-accounts adjustments, tax covenant claims and restraint breaches should sit outside the caps and time bars. An exclusive-remedy clause must carve out fraud and equitable/injunctive relief, and the non-reliance clause cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18) in any event – it should be drafted so it does not purport to, and we should resist any attempt to apply it to the Disclosure Letter itself.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Schedule 7, Clause 8.3)

### 2.1 General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers
The Seller seeks to treat everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the accounts, statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records" as disclosed against all warranties. **Push back:**
- General disclosure of the data room should be accepted only if the data room is indexed, frozen on USB/certified copy at signing, and the disclosure is "fair" disclosure – i.e. with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. A document buried in a folder does not disclose a problem a reasonable reader would not have spotted.
- Public registers should be limited to specific named searches (ASIC company search, PPSR, IP Australia, court registers in named jurisdictions) at a stated date, not open-ended "publicly searchable corporate records."
- Clause [1.4] (no admission of breach, materiality or that any consent is required) is a standard reservation, but combined with the content of paragraphs 2–10 it means the Seller is disclosing *facts* while disclaiming the *conclusions* – leaving the Buyer to carry the risk of the conclusion. That is acceptable only if the matters disclosed are converted into specific indemnities or conditions (see Part 3).

### 2.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion
This is one of the most adverse provisions in the package. As drafted it excludes any claim for matters the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge of, **including matters merely "discoverable" from the data room or public records.** Effects:
- It converts the entire data room into an anti-claim shield regardless of whether disclosure was fair.
- "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – the Buyer loses claims for things it did not actually know but theoretically could have found.
- Advisers' knowledge is imputed to the Buyer.

**Position:** Delete. Fallback: limit to the Buyer's *actual* knowledge of specified named deal-team individuals, derived only from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly provide that knowledge does not prejudice any claim under a specific indemnity. Also include an express term that the Buyer's due diligence does not reduce the Seller's warranty liability (commonly accepted in NSW).

---

## 3. Identified risk items – each should be a condition, price adjustment or specific indemnity, not a general warranty

The pattern in the Disclosure Letter is consistent: each item is disclosed as a bare fact, the Seller declines to confirm the consequence, and the Seller Update then characterises the item as resolved, immaterial or "ordinary course." If we accept general disclosure plus clause 8.3, every one of these becomes unrecoverable. Each is addressed below.

### 3.1 Bluefen contract (DD-002) – approximately 30% of revenue
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue; change-of-control consent required under cl 11.2 with conditions under cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Seller position:** "reasonable endeavours," treat condition as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent."
- **Issues:** (i) A customer that is ~30% of revenue is a value-critical dependency; loss of it alone would justify a material price reduction. (ii) "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard – require "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" with specific steps and a timetable. (iii) The condition must require consent that is **unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived in writing** – not just "written consent" of any kind. (iv) We need to see the current form of any draft consent and understand what cl 11.3 requires (guarantee? pricing concession? minimum term?). (v) Consider a specific indemnity or price retention if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within 12 months of Completion attributable to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m
- **Facts:** Facility outstanding; change-of-control trigger at cl 8.1; discharge mechanics at cl 9.2; not repaid; no discharge of security.
- **Seller position:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Issues:** This is directly inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of debt and encumbered assets, with a lender who holds a change-of-control default right exercisable from Completion. **Reject.** Required position:
 - Repayment of Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow (standard payout letter mechanics), with the AUD 3.2m deducted from the amount payable to the Seller;
 - Delivery at Completion of an executed payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to register discharge within [5] business days) and release of any guarantees;
 - If the Seller insists on post-Completion release, a retention of at least the outstanding amount plus break costs, and a specific indemnity for all amounts under the facility.
 - Confirm the precise payout figure including interest, break costs and fees as at the Completion date, and whether any Seller/director guarantees or cross-collateralisation exist.

### 3.3 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004, DD-010) – IP ownership
- **Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; the ledger shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller position:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment amount; "considered adequate."
- **Issues:** This is not a AUD 180,000 problem; it is an IP title problem. If the fees are unpaid, the Company may not own the materials developed under SOW3, which for an analytics business may be core product. The Seller's note that DD-010 "is not independent bank verification of non-payment" cuts both ways – it is also not verification of payment. Required position:
 - Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full and an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay in favour of the Company covering all Project Materials (SOW1–3 and any variations), with moral rights consents;
 - If not deliverable at Completion, a retention and a specific indemnity (uncapped, or capped at purchase price) covering loss of IP rights, licence fees, re-development cost and third-party claims – not merely the AUD 180,000;
 - IP warranty that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business, not qualified by general disclosure of DD-004;
 - Ask what the SOW3 deliverables actually are and whether they are in production.

### 3.4 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000
- **Facts:** Conditional on Completion and continued employment; omitted from funds flow; on-costs unaddressed.
- **Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller."
- **Issues:** If the Company is the employer, the Company bears the liability (plus superannuation at 12% guarantee, payroll tax in NSW at ~5.45% above threshold, and PAYG withholding mechanics) – and it crystallises on Completion, i.e. on the Buyer's watch. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal these are transaction-related liabilities and should be treated as debt or Seller transaction costs. Required position:
 - Treat the AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs as a deduction from the purchase price (as "Transaction Bonuses" within the Debt definition) or paid by the Seller directly at Completion through the funds flow;
 - Obtain the bonus letters; check whether any "continued employment" condition post-dates Completion (in which case the liability may fall in the post-Completion period and needs an indemnity);
 - Confirm the Company's obligations are discharged, not merely funded.

### 3.5 Data export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Facts:** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps; access, scope and notification obligations unknown; investigation "preliminary."
- **Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Issues:** The Seller cannot characterise the incident as immaterial while also disclosing it has not determined whether access occurred or notification is required. Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must conduct a reasonable and expeditious assessment within 30 days of suspecting an eligible data breach. The incident is in the data room as at 22 September 2026; if the assessment is still "preliminary" on 5 November, that is itself a compliance concern. Business contact details may or may not be exempt depending on context, and the records may include customer personnel (Bluefen?). Required position:
 - Warranty and specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and contractual remedies – outside the cap and basket;
 - Pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, provide the report to the Buyer, and make any required notifications to the OAIC and affected individuals before Completion;
 - Confirm whether the link was revoked, whether access logs exist, whether any customer contract (notably Bluefen) requires notification, and whether cyber insurance has been notified;
 - Consider a condition precedent if the assessment reveals an eligible data breach affecting a major customer.

### 3.6 Office lease (DD-007)
- The disclosure says there is a notification obligation but "does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent." We should read the lease ourselves. If it is notification only, give notice before Completion as a Completion deliverable. If change-of-control constitutes a deemed assignment (common in commercial leases), it is a consent matter and should be a condition or at least a specific indemnity for landlord default/termination.

### 3.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000
- **Facts:** Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each; Seller says "read together"; declines to say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Issues:** The structuring is notable – each item falls well under any materiality threshold a general warranty would carry, but aggregated they are AUD 330,000. Questions: are these renewals of contracts in the ordinary course that would recur annually (so already in the earnings base) or one-off commitments entered pre-Completion that benefit the Seller's period? Are any already accrued and unpaid (in which case they are working capital/debt)? Were they entered into after the locked-box date or during the gap period? Required position: (i) treat any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion as Debt; (ii) ensure the gap-period conduct covenants prohibit new commitments over a threshold without Buyer consent; (iii) expressly aggregate related claims for de minimis purposes.

### 3.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure says the restriction is on *assignment* and not triggered by a share sale. Verify the drafting ourselves – many assignment clauses define assignment to include change of control. If it is assignment-only, no action beyond a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed in a schedule.

### 3.9 Title (DD-012)
- The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and expressly notes the Buyer "has not completed its own verification." A company share register is prima facie evidence but not conclusive. Required steps: current ASIC extract and historical member search; copies of share certificates; check for any option, convertible or employee equity arrangements (the DD-005 bonus participants may have been promised equity); PPSR search against Harbourglass for any security over the shares (relevant given Riverlark – the shares may be charged); confirm Harbourglass's own capacity and board approval. Title warranty to be unqualified and uncapped (see 1.4).

### 3.10 Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"
- Not accepted. Tax should be dealt with by a separate tax indemnity/covenant with a 7-year period and a cap at purchase price, covering pre-Completion tax and the on-costs issues in 3.4. IP warranties need to stand independently given Ironquay. A pre-Completion tax due diligence sign-off (GST, payroll tax, R&D tax incentive if claimed, employee/contractor classification for a data analytics workforce) should be confirmed.

---

## 4. Debt-free / cash-free mechanics – reconciliation

Taking the items above together, the Seller's funds flow appears to understate deductions from the headline price by:

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Treatment sought |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 + break costs | Repaid at Completion from price |
| Completion bonuses | 420,000 + super + payroll tax (~AUD 490k all-in) | Deducted as Debt / Transaction Bonus |
| Ironquay SOW3 fees | 180,000 | Paid at Completion or retained |
| Sandbar renewals (if accrued) | up to 330,000 | Debt / working capital |
| **Indicative aggregate** | **~AUD 4.1–4.2m** | |

Confirm whether the deal is locked-box or completion accounts; either way the Debt, Cash and Working Capital definitions should be reviewed line by line to capture these items.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / walk-away issues**
1. Fundamental, title and capacity warranties: capped at 100% of price, 6+ years, not subject to disclosure. Reject "administrative simplicity."
2. Riverlark: repaid at Completion from the purchase price with release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion. Reject post-Completion release.
3. Clause 8.3 knowledge exclusion: delete; fallback to actual knowledge of named individuals from fairly disclosed matters only.
4. Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance confined to Warranty Claims; carve out fraud, specific indemnities, tax covenant, price-adjustment and ACL claims.

**Specific indemnities (outside cap, basket and 18-month limit)**
5. Ironquay IP – full loss, not limited to AUD 180,000; confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverable.
6. DD-006 data incident – all regulatory, notification and third-party loss; assessment completed and notifications made pre-Completion.
7. Completion bonuses and on-costs – deducted from price or paid by Seller via funds flow.
8. Bluefen – loss if contract terminated or materially re-priced within 12 months due to change of control.

**Conditions precedent**
9. Bluefen consent: unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; "all reasonable endeavours" with defined steps.
10. (Conditional on review) Office lease consent if change of control is a deemed assignment.

**Commercial / limitation package**
11. Cap 30–50% (or 20% only with the carve-outs above and W&I); tipping basket; 24 months; aggregation of related claims; tax 7 years.
12. Disclosure: fair-disclosure standard; frozen indexed data room; public records limited to named searches at a fixed date.

**Due diligence follow-ups before responding**
13. Read Bluefen cl 11.3, Mossvale assignment clause and office lease change-of-control provisions first-hand.
14. Independent title verification: ASIC history, share certificates, PPSR against Harbourglass, options/equity promises.
15. Riverlark payout figure and guarantee structure; Sandbar contracts (timing, accrual, termination rights); DD-006 incident log and OAIC assessment status; bonus letters.

**Procedural**
16. Respond that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation is not accepted, that no clause is agreed until confirmed in writing by the Buyer, and that the Buyer's mark-up will address all clauses.

I am happy to turn this into a formal issues list or draft the mark-up of clauses 8.3, 11.1 and 12 if useful.

- It converts the entire data room into an anti-claim shield regardless of whether disclosure was fair.
- "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – the Buyer loses claims for things it did not actually know but theoretically could have found.
- Advisers' knowledge is imputed to the Buyer.

**Position:** Delete. Fallback: limit to the Buyer's *actual* knowledge of specified named deal-team individuals, derived only from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly provide that knowledge does not prejudice any claim under a specific indemnity. Also include an express term that the Buyer's due diligence does not reduce the Seller's warranty liability (commonly accepted in NSW).

## 3. Identified risk items – each should be a condition, price adjustment or specific indemnity, not a general warranty

The pattern in the Disclosure Letter is consistent: each item is disclosed as a bare fact, the Seller declines to confirm the consequence, and the Seller Update then characterises the item as resolved, immaterial or "ordinary course." If we accept general disclosure plus clause 8.3, every one of these becomes unrecoverable. Each is addressed below.

### 3.1 Bluefen contract (DD-002) – approximately 30% of revenue
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue; change-of-control consent required under cl 11.2 with conditions under cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Seller position:** "reasonable endeavours," treat condition as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent."
- **Issues:** (i) A customer that is ~30% of revenue is a value-critical dependency; loss of it alone would justify a material price reduction. (ii) "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard – require "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" with specific steps and a timetable. (iii) The condition must require consent that is **unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived in writing** – not just "written consent" of any kind. (iv) We need to see the current form of any draft consent and understand what cl 11.3 requires (guarantee? pricing concession? minimum term?). (v) Consider a specific indemnity or price retention if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within 12 months of Completion attributable to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m
- **Facts:** Facility outstanding; change-of-control trigger at cl 8.1; discharge mechanics at cl 9.2; not repaid; no discharge of security.
- **Seller position:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Issues:** This is directly inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of debt and encumbered assets, with a lender who holds a change-of-control default right exercisable from Completion. **Reject.** Required position:
 - Repayment of Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow (standard payout letter mechanics), with the AUD 3.2m deducted from the amount payable to the Seller;
 - Delivery at Completion of an executed payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to register discharge within [5] business days) and release of any guarantees;
 - If the Seller insists on post-Completion release, a retention of at least the outstanding amount plus break costs, and a specific indemnity for all amounts under the facility.
 - Confirm the precise payout figure including interest, break costs and fees as at the Completion date, and whether any Seller/director guarantees or cross-collateralisation exist.

### 3.3 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004, DD-010) – IP ownership
- **Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; the ledger shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller position:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment amount; "considered adequate."
- **Issues:** This is not a AUD 180,000 problem; it is an IP title problem. If the fees are unpaid, the Company may not own the materials developed under SOW3, which for an analytics business may be core product. The Seller's note that DD-010 "is not independent bank verification of non-payment" cuts both ways – it is also not verification of payment. Required position:
 - Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full and an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay in favour of the Company covering all Project Materials (SOW1–3 and any variations), with moral rights consents;
 - If not deliverable at Completion, a retention and a specific indemnity (uncapped, or capped at purchase price) covering loss of IP rights, licence fees, re-development cost and third-party claims – not merely the AUD 180,000;
 - IP warranty that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business, not qualified by general disclosure of DD-004;
 - Ask what the SOW3 deliverables actually are and whether they are in production.

### 3.4 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000
- **Facts:** Conditional on Completion and continued employment; omitted from funds flow; on-costs unaddressed.
- **Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller."
- **Issues:** If the Company is the employer, the Company bears the liability (plus superannuation at 12% guarantee, payroll tax in NSW at ~5.45% above threshold, and PAYG withholding mechanics) – and it crystallises on Completion, i.e. on the Buyer's watch. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal these are transaction-related liabilities and should be treated as debt or Seller transaction costs. Required position:
 - Treat the AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs as a deduction from the purchase price (as "Transaction Bonuses" within the Debt definition) or paid by the Seller directly at Completion through the funds flow;
 - Obtain the bonus letters; check whether any "continued employment" condition post-dates Completion (in which case the liability may fall in the post-Completion period and needs an indemnity);
 - Confirm the Company's obligations are discharged, not merely funded.

### 3.5 Data export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Facts:** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps; access, scope and notification obligations unknown; investigation "preliminary."
- **Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Issues:** The Seller cannot characterise the incident as immaterial while also disclosing it has not determined whether access occurred or notification is required. Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must conduct a reasonable and expeditious assessment within 30 days of suspecting an eligible data breach. The incident is in the data room as at 22 September 2026; if the assessment is still "preliminary" on 5 November, that is itself a compliance concern. Business contact details may or may not be exempt depending on context, and the records may include customer personnel (Bluefen?). Required position:
 - Warranty and specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and contractual remedies – outside the cap and basket;
 - Pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, provide the report to the Buyer, and make any required notifications to the OAIC and affected individuals before Completion;
 - Confirm whether the link was revoked, whether access logs exist, whether any customer contract (notably Bluefen) requires notification, and whether cyber insurance has been notified;
 - Consider a condition precedent if the assessment reveals an eligible data breach affecting a major customer.

### 3.6 Office lease (DD-007)
- The disclosure says there is a notification obligation but "does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent." We should read the lease ourselves. If it is notification only, give notice before Completion as a Completion deliverable. If change-of-control constitutes a deemed assignment (common in commercial leases), it is a consent matter and should be a condition or at least a specific indemnity for landlord default/termination.

### 3.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000
- **Facts:** Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each; Seller says "read together"; declines to say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Issues:** The structuring is notable – each item falls well under any materiality threshold a general warranty would carry, but aggregated they are AUD 330,000. Questions: are these renewals of contracts in the ordinary course that would recur annually (so already in the earnings base) or one-off commitments entered pre-Completion that benefit the Seller's period? Are any already accrued and unpaid (in which case they are working capital/debt)? Were they entered into after the locked-box date or during the gap period? Required position: (i) treat any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion as Debt; (ii) ensure the gap-period conduct covenants prohibit new commitments over a threshold without Buyer consent; (iii) expressly aggregate related claims for de minimis purposes.

### 3.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure says the restriction is on *assignment* and not triggered by a share sale. Verify the drafting ourselves – many assignment clauses define assignment to include change of control. If it is assignment-only, no action beyond a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed in a schedule.

### 3.9 Title (DD-012)
- The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and expressly notes the Buyer "has not completed its own verification." A company share register is prima facie evidence but not conclusive. Required steps: current ASIC extract and historical member search; copies of share certificates; check for any option, convertible or employee equity arrangements (the DD-005 bonus participants may have been promised equity); PPSR search against Harbourglass for any security over the shares (relevant given Riverlark – the shares may be charged); confirm Harbourglass's own capacity and board approval. Title warranty to be unqualified and uncapped (see 1.4).

### 3.10 Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"
- Not accepted. Tax should be dealt with by a separate tax indemnity/covenant with a 7-year period and a cap at purchase price, covering pre-Completion tax and the on-costs issues in 3.4. IP warranties need to stand independently given Ironquay. A pre-Completion tax due diligence sign-off (GST, payroll tax, R&D tax incentive if claimed, employee/contractor classification for a data analytics workforce) should be confirmed.

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Treatment sought |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 + break costs | Repaid at Completion from price |
| Completion bonuses | 420,000 + super + payroll tax (~AUD 490k all-in) | Deducted as Debt / Transaction Bonus |

Confirm whether the deal is locked-box or completion accounts; either way the Debt, Cash and Working Capital definitions should be reviewed line by line to capture these items.

**Non-negotiable / walk-away issues**
1. Fundamental, title and capacity warranties: capped at 100% of price, 6+ years, not subject to disclosure. Reject "administrative simplicity."
2. Riverlark: repaid at Completion from the purchase price with release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion. Reject post-Completion release.
3. Clause 8.3 knowledge exclusion: delete; fallback to actual knowledge of named individuals from fairly disclosed matters only.

7. Completion bonuses and on-costs – deducted from price or paid by Seller via funds flow.
